messages:
Priya Nair: Quick flag — launching the new product cohort yesterday and our weekly pulseboard shows 2x paid leads but SFDC doesn't. Something's off with attribution. :eyes:
Evan Chen: Link?
Priya Nair: https://dash.redwood.ai/marketing/launch-cohort — look at 'paid_cohort' segment and channel breakdown.
Maya Singh: I see it. Direct channel spiked at the same time as the /thanks page redirect. Maybe UTM collapsed.
Liam Park: We swapped the webinar CTA to a direct link (no utm) on the launch post for cleaner URLs. That could be leaking into direct.
Priya Nair: Ugh. That explains it. Can we run a quick query to split by landing_page + referrer?
Evan Chen: Running a one-off now. SQL:
```sql
SELECT landing_page, referrer, count(*) as leads
FROM events
WHERE event_date >= '2026-03-18' AND cohort='launch_paid'
GROUP BY 1,2
ORDER BY 3 DESC
LIMIT 50;
```
analytics-bot: Pipeline 'prod-events' started reprocessing partition 2026-03-18 — ETA ~6m
Maya Singh: If SQL shows most leads with blank utm_source we should re-route to 'web:launch' in Segment mapping and backfill in HubSpot.
Liam Park: I'll put a temporary rule in HubSpot to prefer referrer path when utm_source is null. On it.
Priya Nair: Thanks. Can someone add a note to the weekly KPI doc so the next report flags this as attribution noise? https://docs.redwood.ai/marketing/weekly-kpi
Evan Chen: Added a row in the sheet and a short note. Will post an update in the weekly review tomorrow.
Maya Singh: Follow-up action: revert CTA to include utm_campaign for paid posts, and QA landing redirects. Assign to @Liam and @Maya.
Priya Nair: Perfect. If the backfill closes the gap, we can mark as resolved in the pulseboard. :white_check_mark:
Liam Park: Will update here when HubSpot rule is live — expect within 10m.
